expectations.name: single-function-in-isolation
expected_behavior: Runs straight through with no plan gate, mapping to the `Test_Parse` direct-test family
Measures with `-run '^Test_Parse($|_)'` and reads only `Parse`'s own line range — the coverage `Test_Load` contributes is not counted
Adds table rows aimed at the two error branches, re-measures, and confirms those lines went 0 → hit
New rows follow the style Test rules: `have`/`want`, never `got`; error subtests named `error - <condition>`

expectations.name: package-target-is-plan-first
expected_behavior: States the resolved kind (package) and the function set before measuring
Presents a plan — per-function current coverage, proposed easy cases, deferred and un-coverable lines — and waits for approval before writing anything

Works one function to completion before starting the next — a per-function after-profile exists for each (`<Func>.after`), each written after that function's tests and before the next function's, so the order is visible in the artifacts rather than asserted

expectations.name: deferred-and-uncoverable-are-reported
expected_behavior: Covers the easy lines, defers the network branch with a stated reason, and names the defensive branch un-coverable
Never attempts the un-coverable line
Under `include=all`, builds the fake for the network branch and covers it
Still reports the defensive `return` as un-coverable under `include=all` — the flag does not turn it into an attempt

expectations.name: line-target-resolves-to-its-function
expected_behavior: Resolves the target to `Load` and states the kind (line) and the function
Runs `Load`'s full per-function loop without a plan gate, since a line target is a single function
Measures with `-run '^Test_Load($|_)'`, never with whole-package coverage

expectations.name: module-mode-honors-its-controls
expected_behavior: Touches only `svc` and `api`, leaving the other seven packages alone

Dispatches one subagent per package and merges their reports, listing packages covered and skipped — each worker's per-package report survives on disk, so the fan-out is visible in the artifacts rather than asserted
Adds at most five tests or cases across the whole run and reports what is left under the cap
Each worker finishes and verifies one function before starting the next — its per-function after-profiles exist, one per function it touched

expectations.name: writes-into-existing-tests
expected_behavior: Adds the two new cases as rows in `Test_Encode_tabular`, since they fit the existing table's shape, rather than creating a parallel test function
Keeps the table loop branch-free: the two added rows are driven by the same fields the existing rows use, and no `if` on a row field appears in the loop body
Deletes the now-unused helper from `all_test.go`, and drops the file if nothing is left in it
Ends with `gofmt -l` clean and `go test -v -race` showing `--- PASS` for every test in the edited files

expectations.name: terse-output
expected_behavior: Opens with the result — no preamble and no narration of measuring
Reports the before → after coverage delta, the tests added, and any deferred or un-coverable lines, each stated once
No closing restatement of the table it just showed
Reports the gate as a result, not a log: the reply gives the pass/fail outcome per edited package and quotes no `go test` output beyond it

expectations.name: no-seam-stays-deferred-under-include-all
expected_behavior: Adds cases only inside `*_test.go`, the skill's whole write scope, and edits no file under the production package — the fixture's non-test files are byte-identical after the run
Leaves the POST-failure branch deferred even under `include=all`: the flag authorizes building fakes, not editing production code
Names what the seam would be, so the author can decide, rather than adding one unasked
Does not report the function as fully covered

expectations.name: missing-test-family-is-not-zero-percent
expected_behavior: Notices that `-run '^Test_Normalize($|_)'` matched nothing — `no tests to run`, exit 0 — rather than reading the result as a measured 0%
Reports the function as uncovered and scaffolds `Test_Normalize`
Does not credit the off-convention `TestNormalizeHelper` as the family

expectations.name: unrecognized-control-token
expected_behavior: Says `only=exported` is not a control this skill has, and names the ones it does
Does not silently ignore it, and does not invent the filter it sounds like — a run that quietly drops an argument leaves the user thinking it applied
Honours `max_tests=4`, which is a real control, and proceeds with defaults for the rest
Reports what is left under the cap
